01Before the day

Setup checklist

Your ticks are saved in this browser only.

02Preparation

Prepare at your level

New to architecture documentation

About 30 to 45 minutes:

  • Skim the twelve arc42 sections and read what each one is for
  • Try one Mermaid diagram in the live editor
  • Think of a system you know well and who uses it

Experienced engineer or architect

About 60 to 90 minutes:

  • Read the arc42 guidance for sections 5 and 9, and a sample ADR
  • Bring a real constraint, quality goal and trade-off from your own work
  • Look at one docs-as-code example and decide what you would change

05Template

Team skeleton

Paste this into arc42-team.md on the day.

# <System name> — arc42 skeleton
## 1. Introduction and Goals
### 1.1 Requirements overview
### 1.2 Quality goals (top 3–5, each with a scenario)
### 1.3 Stakeholders (role, expectation)
## 2. Constraints (ID, constraint, why, effect)
## 3. Context and Scope
### 3.1 Business context (diagram)
### 3.2 Technical context (table)
## 4. Solution Strategy (goal, approach, why, trade-off)
## 5. Building Block View
### 5.1 Level 1 (diagram + table)
### 5.2 Contract: <block>
## 6. Runtime View (scenario + failure branch)
## 7. Deployment View (environments, mapping table)
## 8. Crosscutting Concepts
## 9. Architecture Decisions (ADR-0001…)
## 10. Quality Requirements (tree + scenarios)
## 11. Risks and Technical Debt
## 12. Glossary

06Vocabulary

Key terms

Stakeholder and concern
A stakeholder is anyone with an interest in the system. A concern is something they care about, such as recovering a lost order.
Quality scenario
A testable statement of stimulus, response and metric, such as “95% of confirmations appear within 3 s at 300 orders per minute”.
Container and component
A container is something you start: an application or data store. A component is a grouping of related functionality behind an interface inside a container.
Contract
What a block promises and expects: pre-conditions, post-conditions, invariants and error modes.
ADR
An architecture decision record: one significant decision with its context, options, decision and consequences.
Idempotency
Repeating a request has the same effect as doing it once.

07Ground rules

Rules for AI today

Write a human draft first. Then ask AI why, and what’s missing, not only to write it. You decide: give every AI line a verdict of accepted, rejected or edited, with a reason. Use only your workshop case, and never paste passwords, keys, personal data or client-confidential details.

08Self-check

Check before you leave

09After

Your 30 days

Week 1: finish sections 1–4 with your real team. Week 2: sections 5–6, one contract per critical block. Week 3: three ADRs, five scenarios, risks. Week 4: try the agent experiment (no docs, a short index plus two contracts, or the full arc42) and share what you find.
